original_question: Which finite almost simple groups are the automorphism groups of regular polytopes of rank 3? In other words, which finite almost simple groups are generated by three involutions two of which commute? This question has been answered for finite simple groups; see 7.30 in Archive. Ya.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.101 in the New Problems (21st issue, 2026) section: determine which finite almost simple groups occur as automorphism groups of regular polytopes of rank 3, equivalently which finite almost simple groups are generated by three involutions, two of which commute. The problem itself adds that the finite simple-group case is covered by Archive Problem 7.30. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official wording. It correctly keeps the scope to finite almost simple groups, preserves the rank-3 regular-polytope formulation, includes the paper’s own equivalent reformulation via three involutions with two commuting, and correctly notes the cross-reference to the finite simple-group case in Archive Problem 7.30. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, define a finite almost simple group as a finite group G with non-abelian finite simple socle T such that T ≤ G ≤ Aut(T).
State explicitly that the task is to classify groups up to isomorphism that occur as the full automorphism group of some regular polytope of rank 3.
If maximum self-containment is desired, gloss a regular polytope of rank 3 as a regular polyhedron.
If one wants the algebraic reformulation maximally explicit, say that an involution means an element of order 2.
There are no ambient field/ring, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic-quantifier conditions here; this is a pure finite-group classification problem.
refined_question: Classify the finite almost simple groups G — that is, finite groups with non-abelian finite simple socle T satisfying T ≤ G ≤ Aut(T) — that occur, up to isomorphism, as the full automorphism groups of regular polytopes of rank 3; equivalently, determine exactly which such groups G admit a generating triple of involutions ρ0, ρ1, ρ2 with two of them commuting.
equivalent_formulation: Determine exactly which finite almost simple groups can be generated by three involutions, two of which commute. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The nearest official formulation is Problem 21.101, and your draft is essentially a near-verbatim transcription of it. So the right refinement is not to broaden the problem, but only to make it self-contained by adding the standard definition of almost simple and by clarifying that one is asking for occurrence up to isomorphism as a full automorphism group. I kept the paper’s exact scope and its explicit equivalent reformulation, and I did not drift to broader questions about all finite groups, higher-rank polytopes, or related string C-group classification problems. The final sentence of your draft is also faithful to the paper’s own cross-reference to Archive Problem 7.30; the archive entry records the finite simple-group case as known mod CFSG. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
